text:
maria: Heads-up — planning the tenant-priority routing switchover for next week. Need a canary + safety plan that avoids oscillation (flip-flopping slices) and keeps P95 tails stable. Thoughts?
alex: Goals? acceptance criteria? what are our hard stops (latency, errors, cost)?
maria: primary: no P95 increase > 15% vs baseline, error rate < 0.1% absolute, unit cost delta < 8%. secondary: no customer-visible degradation for top 20 tenants.
cheng: propose a 3-stage approach: 1) micro-cohorts (Goldilocks slices) at 0.5/1/2% for smoke, 2) hold periods with automated stability checks, 3) gradual ramp with oscillation damping.
sam: metrics to gate on: P50/P95/P99 latency, 500/502/429 rate, tail token cost, and request queueing depth. Need anomaly windows (5m and 1h).
alex: I want the flag semantics spelled out. Suggest feature flag with phases + decay TTL + min_hold. Example config: 
```
flag: TENANT_ROUTING_V2
phases:
  - pct: 0.5
    duration: 30m
    min_hold: 30m
  - pct: 2
    duration: 2h
    min_hold: 1h
  - pct: 10
    duration: 6h
    min_hold: 2h
circuit_break: {error_rate: 0.1, p95_increase: 0.15}
oscillation_guard: {decay_secs: 7200}
```
maria: that looks good. add tenant-exempt list for customers we've promised stability to. also require canary alert to page SRE if circuit_break tripped.
devops-bot: flag TENANT_ROUTING_V2 created by maria (env: staging). :white_check_mark:
ops: rollback path needs to be explicit. if circuit_break fires, routing should fallback to ROUTING_LEGACY with deterministic sticky mapping. Also require quick toggle in Console + api.
cheng: rollout steps (short):
- create canary flag (done)
- run micro-cohorts in staging (0.5/1%) 24h smoke
- run 48h hold on 2% with synthetic and real traffic mix
- enable 10% with 2h min_hold, monitor 1h and 4h windows
- decide go/no-go for global ramp after 72h stable
sam: A/B question: do we do A/B (split routing) for a 5% holdback to measure quality delta vs canary? my preference: yes — reserve 5% holdback cohort for A/B with metric diffs.
alex: owners and runbook? who pages during nights?
maria: owners: cheng (canary lead), sam (telemetry), alex (rollback + flag ops). on-call SRE handles paging. Runbook link will be added to the ticket. Timeline: start Tuesday 09:00 UTC, micro-cohorts first 6h, full schedule in ticket.
alex: ok. please add synthetic test IDs and the sample queries we'll run. also bake in a cool-down window between ramps (:hourglass:).
maria: will add tests and runbook. thanks everyone — proceed after I update the ticket and post final flag JSON. :thumbsup:
